idea_goal_statement.description: Define the goal of the project and what the application is
idea_goal_statement.value: An internal platform that makes the delivery, management, and communication of client projects more efficient. It uses Claude-powered agents to turn a client brief into a structured, staged workflow — generating key documents (clarification emails, position documents, scope documents, specialist briefs) at each stage, while keeping humans in control of every client- and specialist-facing conversation. Initial build covers Stages 1-5 of a 10-stage pipeline: Intake, Get Clarifications from Client, Triage, and Review with Specialist Leads.

vibe_style.description: Describe the desired aesthetic, feeling, or tone of the application
vibe_style.value: Clean, efficient, professional — built from scratch with no existing design system. Genuinely well-designed rather than purely functional, since ease of use directly drives adoption by internal account and delivery teams who could otherwise bypass the tool.

audience_definition.description: Define exactly who the application is designed for
audience_definition.value: Two internal user groups at a creative/marketing agency: Client Engagement (Account Managers, Account Directors) who own client relationships, and Delivery (Project Managers at Student/Junior/Mid/Senior levels) who run projects day to day.

problem_solved.description: Briefly state the pain point this app alleviates
problem_solved.value: Project scoping and setup today relies on ad hoc documents, emails, and inconsistent manual processes with no shared structure or historical record. This makes early-stage project delivery slow, inconsistent, and hard to track across a lifecycle that can span days, weeks, or months.

socioeconomic_contextual_factors.description: Include details about the users, their environment, preferences, or specific factors the app must accommodate
socioeconomic_contextual_factors.value: ~90% desktop usage, ~10% mobile (for on-the-go status checks/approvals) — build desktop-first. Users span junior to senior PM levels, so the UX must require no training. Real client briefs are confidential; the pilot uses anonymized seed data (Hub: 'Caroline'; Clients: 'Fizzy', 'Coffee', 'Tooth') until IT/security approves real client data in the platform.

workflow_description.description: Outline the sequence of steps a typical user takes
steps: AM/PM manually uploads or pastes a client brief (deck, Word doc, PDF, email, or call transcript) to start a new Project under a Hub > Client > Workstream
Intake Agent classifies the brief type, extracts what it can, and generates 3 artifacts: a draft Clarification Email, a Project Position Document, and a Project Set-Up Checklist
AM sends the clarification email externally (outside the platform); once the client responds, the PM pastes the client's reply back into the platform as freeform notes
An extraction step updates the Project Position Document (new version), resolving gaps flagged earlier and separating genuine unknowns from client-flagged 'still deciding' items

Triage Agent generates a Draft Scope Document (objectives, deliverables, milestones, roles & responsibilities, budget, assumptions/constraints) from the Position Doc, proceeding even with gaps but flagging them clearly for specialists
PM shares the Draft Scope Document with Specialist Leads (outside the platform), then pastes their feedback back in as freeform notes

An extraction step generates the Deliverables + Services Document: a Deliverables list, a Services table across fixed capabilities (Experience/Creative, Business, Architecture, Tech and Data, Orchestration, Other [free text]), Open Questions/Risks, and Outstanding Gaps Carried Forward
At every point, the PM/AM can see which Stage a project is currently in, tick off manual checklist items, and browse every previously generated document and version

ai_agent_architecture.description: How each 'Agent' named in the workflow is actually built - not autonomous/free-roaming bots, but narrow, single-purpose functions with fixed inputs and structured outputs
principles: One dedicated module per agent (e.g. intake-agent.ts, triage-agent.ts) - each independently buildable, testable, and improvable without touching the others

Structured output, not free text - each agent returns a defined JSON shape matching the exact fields designed for its artifact (e.g. budget, gaps, deliverables as named fields), not prose the app has to parse
Multi-step logic split into separate sequential Claude calls where it helps accuracy (e.g. Intake Agent: classify brief type, THEN extract fields for that type, as two calls rather than one)
No heavyweight agent/orchestration framework - direct calls to the Anthropic API from backend functions is sufficient at this scale and keeps the codebase simple to read and debug
Each parent task in the implementation plan maps to one agent: define its prompt, define its output structure, wire it up, test it
agents_in_scope_for_mvp: Clarification Extraction step (freeform client reply -> updated Position Document)
Triage Agent (Position Document + clarification -> Draft Scope Document)
Specialist Review Extraction step (freeform specialist notes -> Deliverables + Services Document)
Project Brain Chatbot (project-scoped Q&A over that project's documents and knowledge items)

knowledge_base_and_chatbot.description: Two related, cross-cutting capabilities that sit alongside the staged workflow rather than inside a single stage
knowledge_base_and_chatbot.ad_hoc_knowledge_upload: Users can upload documents or paste meeting notes at any time, on any project, regardless of current Stage. Stored as a new 'Knowledge Item' entity: project_id, type, title, content/file, uploaded_by, uploaded_at. Distinct from the versioned Stage Documents (which are agent-generated pipeline artifacts) - Knowledge Items are supplementary and unstructured.
knowledge_base_and_chatbot.project_scoped_chatbot: A per-project Q&A interface. When a user asks a question (e.g. 'what is the delivery date?'), the backend assembles context from ONLY that project's data - its Stage Documents, checklist state, touchpoint notes, and Knowledge Items - filtered by project_id at the database query level. That filtered context plus the question is sent to Claude for an answer.
knowledge_base_and_chatbot.cross_project_isolation_guarantee: Isolation between projects (even within the same Client) is enforced structurally, not just by prompting: every query the chatbot runs is scoped with a project_id WHERE clause at the database layer, so another project's data is never retrieved into context in the first place - there is nothing for the model to leak, because it is never given it.
knowledge_base_and_chatbot.scaling_note_for_later: For pilot scale, assembling all of a project's documents/notes directly into the Claude context window on each question is simple and reliable. If a project accumulates a very large volume of notes/documents over many months, a Level 2 enhancement would add a semantic-search step - still strictly scoped to that one project_id - rather than passing everything in every time.

level_1_mvp.description: Minimal Viable Product - Stages 1-5 of the full pipeline only

features: Multi-format brief ingestion for Intake (Word, PDF, PPTX, pasted text/transcript)
Intake Agent: classify brief type, extract known/unknown fields, generate Clarification Email draft + Project Position Document + Project Set-Up Checklist
Freeform note capture at every human touchpoint (Get Clarifications, Review with Specialist Leads) feeding the next agent
Triage Agent: generate Draft Scope Document from Position Doc + clarification notes; proceed regardless of gaps, flag them clearly
Specialist-review note capture -> generate Deliverables + Services Document
Project Stage Tracker: visual current-stage status per project across the pipeline
Outputs Library: every generated artifact kept and browsable, versioned at each stage transition (not per-edit)
Manual tick-box checklist for project set-up tasks (no external system integration yet)
Hub -> Client -> Workstream -> Project taxonomy, seeded with Hub 'Caroline' and Clients 'Fizzy', 'Coffee', 'Tooth', with room for future bespoke per-client structure
Simple email/password authentication; two role types (Client Engagement, Delivery)
Ad-hoc knowledge upload: documents or meeting notes can be added at any time, on any project, building a running project knowledge base independent of the staged workflow

Project Brain Chatbot: per-project natural-language Q&A (e.g. 'what is the delivery date?') answered strictly from that project's own documents and uploaded knowledge - never another project's, even within the same Client

key_inputs.description: Define what data the user provides
inputs: Client brief (file upload or pasted text, any format)
Freeform notes pasted after client/specialist conversations
Ad-hoc meeting notes/documents uploaded at any time
Natural-language questions asked to the project chatbot

outputs: Project Position Document (versioned, with 'What We Know' / 'What We Need to Find Out' / 'Client-Flagged Open Items' sections)
Per-project Stage status and full document/version history
Chatbot answers grounded only in the specific project's documents and knowledge items

level_2_platform_enhancements.description: Features that enhance the core product, focusing on storage, management, and tracking

features: Bespoke per-client onboarding/configuration flow (structure overrides beyond the baseline taxonomy)
Auto-ingestion of briefs (email forwarding, Teams/SharePoint integration) instead of manual upload
Notifications/automated triggers for checklist items (e.g. auto-notify whoever raises job codes)
Company SSO (Microsoft/Azure AD) authentication
Integration with the organization's actual resource-management 'Workbook' tool

level_3_future_complexity.description: Ambitious, complex features - Stages 6-10 of the full pipeline

features: Estimation Kick Off Agent (Stage 6) and Estimation Session capture (Stage 7)
Commercials Builder Agent (Stage 8), including Statement of Work generation as a Word (.docx) artifact from an existing client-specific baseline template
Planning Agent + Capability Briefing Agent running in parallel (Stage 9) - requires supporting multiple concurrent documents/threads within one stage
Commercial Status Agent (Stage 10) - a recurring/ongoing monitoring stage producing dated snapshots, not a one-time gate
Multi-client bespoke taxonomy variants beyond the baseline Hub > Client > Workstream > Project structure

system_prompt_rules.description: Writing rules or documentation the AI should adhere to
rules: Never auto-send client-facing emails or documents - every client-facing artifact is a draft for human review before it leaves the platform

Always separate genuine gaps in agency understanding from items the client themselves flagged as still-deciding (TBC / '???' / 'add number') - these are semantically different and must stay in separate sections
Version documents at stage transitions, not on every edit, to keep history meaningful
Use only anonymized/test client data (Hub 'Caroline', Clients 'Fizzy'/'Coffee'/'Tooth') until security/IT sign-off for real client data
Never hardcode secrets (API keys, DB connection strings) in code or commit them to git - environment variables only, via .env.local which is gitignored
The 'Services' capability list is fixed for now: Experience/Creative, Business, Architecture, Tech and Data, Orchestration, Other (with a free-text label for Other)
Every database query behind the chatbot must filter by project_id - never assemble or expose data from more than one project in a single chatbot response, even for projects under the same Client
